cards.design_implication: Research designs should incorporate computational or experimental methods capable of resolving interlayer sliding energy barriers to differentiate BN from graphene-like materials.
does_not_establish: Generalizability of this mechanism to other 2D materials not studied in this paper.
Quantitative sliding coefficients for all possible strain states.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We attribute this difference to the distinct interlayer interactions and hence sliding tendencies in these two materials under indentation.
limitations: The claim is limited to the specific comparison between BN and graphene under indentation conditions.
cards.statement: The mechanical strength of BN nanosheets is attributed to strong interlayer interactions that prevent sliding under indentation, unlike graphene.

cards.design_implication: The measurement setup should utilize AFM indentation on nanosheets suspended over micro-wells, with data analysis based on the combined linear and cubic load-displacement relationship.
does_not_establish: Accuracy limits of the AFM technique for thicknesses outside the range tested (1L-9L).
cards.evidence_excerpt: The mechanical properties of the mono- and few-layer graphene and BN nanosheets were studied by indentation at the centre of the suspended regions using AFM.
limitations: Measurability is contingent on the nanosheets being suspended and the region being free of defects.
The excerpt describes the method but does not explicitly define the calibration constants for the specific instrument used in the text provided.
cards.statement: Mechanical properties (elastic modulus and breaking strength) of suspended mono- and few-layer BN nanosheets are measurable via AFM indentation using a pre-fitted load-displacement model.

cards.design_implication: Instrument calibration protocols for force measurements should include both thermal noise and Sader methods to ensure accuracy for high-strength membrane testing.
does_not_establish: The tip deflection calibration method, though separate from spring constant, is often related.
The lateral force calibration for the instrument.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The spring constants of the cantilevers were determined using a combination of the thermal noise method and the Sader method.
limitations: The excerpt does not provide the specific numerical values of the spring constants obtained.
cards.statement: AFM cantilever spring constants were determined using a combination of the thermal noise method and the Sader method.

cards.design_implication: Mechanical property predictions for BN should account for a boundary condition where strength scaling differs from simple linear thickness addition up to 9 layers, contrasting with graphene behavior.
does_not_establish: The mechanical behavior of BN nanosheets with more than 9 layers.
Whether the strength remains constant indefinitely.
cards.evidence_excerpt: In contrast to graphene, whose strength decreases dramatically with an increase in thickness, few-layer BN nanosheets (at least up to 9L) have a strength similar to that of 1L BN.
limitations: The excerpt explicitly limits the finding to thicknesses 'at least up to 9L'.
It specifies the context is comparison to graphene's decrease in strength.
cards.statement: Experimental data confirms that the mechanical strength of BN nanosheets remains stable and insensitive to increasing layer number up to at least 9 layers.
